rv.q: It’s a consoling parable for fractured and blended families everywhere, leaving audiences with a warm and fuzzy feeling of happiness.
Enough to answer to the description of sure-fire hit, my dears.

This Mrs Doubtfire musical review can report that the show strikes a close-to-perfect balance between re-creating the movie’s most memorable scenes and finding a new theatrical language for this zany tale.
Only this genuinely funny comedy musical doesn't feel like a cash grab, thanks to its twenty-first-century jokes, perfectly paced book, and silly voices galore.
Vick's performance, however, gives it all the electricity it needs to achieve lift-off.
The whole piece zips along without breath (thank you director Jerry Zaks).

Gabriel Vick steps into the sizeable shoes of Robin Williams as the exuberant but unreliable voiceover artist, Daniel, who disguises himself as an elderly Scottish nanny to gain access to his kids during a traumatic separation. Vick is terrific, giving a firecracker of a performance in Jerry Zaks’s staging.

The show may delight a younger generation encountering the story for the first time but it ultimately serves as a cautionary tale against taking a well-loved film and giving it a bland treatment on stage.
Well, my dears, the truth is that Mrs Doubtfire is this summer’s sizzling-hot ticket.
Luckily, the show extends into January, so take the whole family and you’ll be guaranteed to leave with a skip in your step.
Not only is it a fantastically fun night out, it has heart...and that alone is worth the ticket price.
It’s supremely daft, foolish fun and gives theatregoers an opportunity to marvel at the timing and stagecraft of a lead who (like Andy Karl in Groundhog Day) earns every dime of his pay check.
This type of schmaltz is often unbearable to sit through but here it’s a joy.

This is probably the most demanding male central role in a musical comedy since Barnum, and he is giving a star-making performance that should, if there’s any justice, catapult him to the top of every casting director’s list of go-to leading men for the foreseeable future.
The real draw is Vick, a super-talented, five-star performer.
Mrs. Doubtfire The Musical is the fun night out you never knew you needed.

cn.t: Critics find this film-to-musical adaptation surprisingly successful, with Gabriel Vick earning widespread praise for stepping into Robin Williams' iconic role. While some dismiss it as nostalgia-bait, most applaud its energy, humor, and smart updates.

vr.q: I think if it's possible what we're looking at here is a good show that is not a good musical
